newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends up in line with surge in JGBs.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends up in line with surge in JGBs.

text.p: The key September Euroyen futures contract ended higher on Wednesday in line with a sharp rise in Japanese government bonds.
The September reached as high as 99.31 late in the afternoon, as JGBs gained upward momentum near the close, a trader for a major brokerage house said.
A fall in interest rate swap (IRS) rates triggered the rise in JGBs and Euroyen futures, a city bank trader said.
Japanese banks were said to have received fixed interest rates in the two- and three-year zones, the city bank trader said.
The two-year IRS rate stood at 0.82/86 percent as of 0704 GMT, down from previous day's 0.85/89 percent. The three-year IRS rate stood at 1.19/23 percent, down from 1.23/27 percent.
The September Euroyen futures contract moved within a range of 99.27 to 99.31. Turnover was 52,015 contracts.
The rise in JGBs was considered a more significant factor for Euroyen futures than weakness in Tokyo share prices, a trader for another brokerage house said.
The weakness in share prices had not led to a fall in JGBs on Wednesday, and therefore did not have a depressing effect on Euroyen futures, the trader said.
There has been speculation in the bond market that the recent falls in the Tokyo stock market may force investors to sell cash JGBs to lock in profits and cover losses from their stock holdings.
Other traders said weakness in the Tokyo stock market would probably force the Bank of Japan to maintain its current policy of low interest rates, and was a supportive factor for Euroyen futures.
The Bank of Japan drained a net 200 billion yen from the money market on Wednesday, maintaining its neutral stance.
The weighted average of the key overnight call rate was likely to be unchanged from the previous day at 0.49 percent, a trust bank trader said.
About 80 billion yen worth of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were issued at 0.53 percent.
About 140 billion yen of one-month CDs and 30 billion yen worth of two-month CDs were issued at 0.51 percent.
All CD rates were unchanged from Tuesday.
